---
id: "smk-19"
title: "The Amazon"
---

The Amazon is the largest river in the world by discharge and by the area of its drainage basin, and it rivals the Nile in length. It rises in the Andes of Peru and flows east across Brazil for roughly 6,400 kilometres to the Atlantic Ocean, where its mouth is more than 300 kilometres wide. The river carries about a fifth of all the fresh water that reaches the oceans. Its basin, covering some seven million square kilometres, holds the largest tropical rainforest on Earth and an extraordinary variety of fish, mammals, birds and plants. The Amazon has hundreds of tributaries, several of which, such as the Madeira, the Negro and the Tapajós, are among the largest rivers in the world in their own right. Ocean-going ships can sail upstream as far as Manaus, about 1,500 kilometres from the sea. Seasonal floods raise the water level by many metres and inundate vast areas of forest.
